content: 1. Sarecycline and P-gp Inhibitors: When sarecycline is co-administered with P-glycoprotein (P-gp) inhibitors, the levels or effects of P-gp substrates, such as carvedilol, ceritinib, cetirizine, and others, may increase. This could lead to toxicities. Close monitoring is required, and dosage adjustments may be necessary. 2. Sarecycline and Cholera Vaccine: Sarecycline may antagonize the effects of the cholera vaccine due to pharmacodynamic interactions. Avoid co-administration of systemic antibiotics, including sarecycline, with the cholera vaccine, as these antibiotics may inactivate the vaccine strain. Do not administer the vaccine to patients who have received antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 3. Sarecycline and Bile Acid Sequestrants (e.g., cholestyramine, colesevelam, colestipol): These agents can reduce the absorption of sarecycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal (GI) absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate dosing by at least 2 hours and monitor for reduced efficacy of sarecycline. 4. Sarecycline and Multivalent Cation-Containing Products (e.g., ferric carboxymaltose, ferrous sulfate, ferrous fumarate, ferric citrate): These products may impair the absorption of sarecycline, leading to decreased efficacy. Separate the administration of sarecycline and these products by at least 2 hours. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 5. Sarecycline and Chromium or Copper: These elements can reduce the absorption of sarecycline when taken orally. Separate dosing and monitor for reduced therapeutic effects. 6. Sarecycline and Citric Acid/Sodium Bicarbonate: This combination may decrease the absorption of sarecycline. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 7. Sarecycline and Cisatracurium: Sarecycline may enhance the effects of cisatracurium through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 8. Sarecycline and Penicillins (e.g., dicloxacillin): Sarecycline may interfere with the bactericidal action of penicillins due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration or monitor for reduced therapeutic effects of penicillins. 9. Sarecycline and P-gp Substrates (e.g., digoxin, diltiazem, docetaxel, doxorubicin, cyclosporine, everolimus, etc.): Sarecycline can increase the levels or effects of these drugs by inhibiting P-gp efflux transporters. This may lead to toxicities. Use caution, monitor closely, and consider dosage adjustments. 10. Sarecycline and Anticoagulants (e.g., dabigatran, edoxaban): Sarecycline may increase the levels or effects of these anticoagulants via P-gp inhibition, potentially increasing the risk of bleeding. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 11. Sarecycline and Antineoplastic Agents (e.g., crizotinib, idarubicin, imatinib): Sarecycline may increase the levels or effects of these agents by inhibiting P-gp transporters. Monitor for toxicities and adjust dosages as necessary. 12. Sarecycline and Antihistamines (e.g., desloratadine, fexofenadine): Sarecycline may increase the levels or effects of these antihistamines via P-gp inhibition. Monitor for potential toxicities and adjust therapy as needed. 13. Sarecycline and Corticosteroids (e.g., dexamethasone, hydrocortisone): Sarecycline may increase the levels or effects of corticosteroids by inhibiting P-gp transporters. Monitor closely for toxicities and adjust dosages if required. 14. Sarecycline and Antiviral Agents (e.g., indinavir, glecaprevir/pibrentasvir): Sarecycline may increase the levels or effects of these antiviral agents via P-gp inhibition. Monitor for toxicities and adjust therapy as needed. 15. Sarecycline and Erythromycin Derivatives (e.g., erythromycin base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, stearate): Sarecycline may increase the levels or effects of these antibiotics by inhibiting P-gp transporters. Monitor closely for toxicities and adjust therapy as necessary. 16. Sarecycline and Iodine: Iodine may reduce the absorption of sarecycline when taken orally. Separate dosing and monitor for reduced efficacy.
